body.text:
nityakarmapūjāvidhiḥ
oṃ namaḥ śrīvajrasattvāya |
body.translated_text: <s>Nityakarmapūjāvidhi</s> (Procedure for Daily Ritual Worship). <s>OṂ</s>, homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

body.text: atha nityakarmapūjāvidhiḥ prārabhyate | tatrādau oṃ hrīṃ svāhā 3 kāyaviśodhane svāhā | iti mantreṇa tridhā ācamya pūjābhāṇḍasaṃkalpaṃ kuryāt | tadyathā - oṃ adya śrīmacchrītyādinā saṃkalpoccāraṇānantaramidaṃ mantraṃ paṭhet | oṃ namo bhagavate puṣpaketurājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | tadyathā - oṃ puṣpe 2 mahāpuṣpe supuṣpe puṣpodbhave puṣpasaṃbhave puṣpāvakiraṇe svāhā | idaṃ sapuṣpadhūpadīpa gandharasanaivedyādiyuktaṃ suvarṇapuṣpabhājanaṃ saṃkalpayāmyaham | tato prāṇāyāmādi nyāsayogādi kṛtvā guruṃ ca namaskṛtya śaṅkhaṃ pūjayet || oṃ gurubhyo namaḥ 3 samasta guru ājñā | oṃ ā hūṃ vaṃ vajrodake hūṃ svāhā || śirasi śaṅkhodakenābhiṣiñcet -
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Nityakarmapūjāvidhi</s> (procedure for daily ritual worship) begins. Therein, first one should sip water three times with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>OṂ HRĪṂ SVĀHĀ</s>' (three times), '<s>kāyaviśodhane svāhā</s>' (for the purification of the body), and then make the formal resolution (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) for the worship implements. Namely, after uttering the resolution beginning with '<s>OṂ</s>, today, O glorious...' and so forth, one should recite this <s>mantra</s>: '<s>OṂ</s>, homage to the Blessed One, <s>Puṣpaketurāja Tathāgata</s>, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Namely: <s>OṂ puṣpe puṣpe mahāpuṣpe supuṣpe puṣpodbhave puṣpasaṃbhave puṣpāvakiraṇe svāhā</s>.' 'I make the formal resolution for this golden flower-vessel equipped with flowers, incense, lamp, perfume, food-offerings, and the rest.' Then, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) and <s>nyāsa</s> (placement of mantras on the body) and the rest, and having saluted the <s>guru</s>, one should worship the conch shell. '<s>OṂ</s>, homage to the <s>gurus</s>' (three times). 'The command of all <s>gurus</s>.' '<s>OṂ Ā HŪṂ VAṂ vajrodake HŪṂ SVĀHĀ</s>.' One should sprinkle the head with conch-shell water:

children.translated_text: Just as all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> were bathed immediately upon birth,
so shall I bathe with pure divine water.

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamaśriye hūṃ | punaḥ | omhrī svāheti mantreṇācamya pūrvoktamantreṇa pūjābhāṇḍamadhiṣṭhāya puṣpaikaṃ trikāyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā bhūmau nyaset | oṃ āḥ huṃ 3 tiṣṭha vajrāsane huṃ | pārśvābhyāṃ kṣipet dvau puṣpau | oṃ sarvapāpānapanaya huṃ | ekaṃ śirasi nyasedanena mantreṇa - oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca huṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā | maṇḍale tilakaṃ kṛtvātmānaṃ ca bhūṣayet | oṃ vajratilakabhūṣaṇe svāhā | sajalapuṣpākṣatavāsamaṇḍale pātayedanena mantreṇa, oṃ vajrodake hūṃ | oṃ vajragomaye huṃ | oṃ vajrabhūmau surekhe sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhitiṣṭhantu svāhā | etacca paṭhet |
body.translated_text: '<s>OṂ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamaśriye HŪṂ</s>.' Again, having sipped water with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>OṂ HRĪ SVĀHĀ</s>,' having empowered the worship vessel with the aforementioned <s>mantra</s>, one should place a single flower on the ground as the establishment of the three bodies (<s>trikāyādhiṣṭhāna</s>). '<s>OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ</s>' (three times), '<s>tiṣṭha vajrāsane HŪṂ</s>' (remain on the vajra seat). One should cast two flowers on either side: '<s>OṂ sarvapāpānapanaya HŪṂ</s>' (remove all sins). One should place one on the head with this <s>mantra</s>: '<s>OṂ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ</s>.' Having made a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) on the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should adorn oneself: '<s>OṂ vajratilakabhūṣaṇe SVĀHĀ</s>.' On the <s>maṇḍala</s> with water, flowers, unbroken rice, and sandalwood paste, one should drop with this <s>mantra</s>: '<s>OṂ vajrodake HŪṂ</s>,' '<s>OṂ vajragomaye HŪṂ</s>,' '<s>OṂ vajrabhūmau surekhe sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhitiṣṭhantu SVĀHĀ</s>.' And one should recite this:

children.text: dānaṃ gomayambunā ca sahitaṃ śīlaṃ ca sammārjanaṃ
children.translated_text: Giving is [represented by] cow dung mixed with water; morality is the sweeping;
patience is the removal of small ants; effort is the establishment of the ritual action;
<s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the one-pointed concentration at that moment; wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the beautiful line, radiant —

children.text: etāḥ pāramitā ṣaḍeva labhate kṛtvā munermaṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: these six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are obtained by making the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the Sage.
One becomes golden in complexion, freed from all diseases,
distinguished among gods and humans, with a radiance shining like the moon;
one is born in a royal lineage, endowed with wealth and gold,
having performed bodily actions in this excellent abode of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha).

body.text: oṃ sule(re)khe sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhitiṣṭhantu svāhā | puṣpaikaṃ hastasyopari nyasya nyubjahastaṃ kṛtvā maṇḍale kṣipet | oṃ candrārkavimale svāhā | maṇḍalaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya puṣpaikaṃ balibhāṇḍe kṣipet | oṃ vajrasattva sarvavighnānutsādaya huṃ | pūrvādikrameṇa dviparivartanaṃ kṛtvā ekaviṃśatipuṣpapātanaṃ kuryāt maṇḍale | oṃ haḥ mahāmadhye merave namaḥ | oṃ hrīṃ madhye merave namaḥ | oṃ sūṃ sūkṣmamadhye merave namaḥ | iti madhye | oṃ yaṃ pūrvavidehāya namaḥ | pū | oṃ raṃ jambūdvīpāya namaḥ | da | oṃ laṃ aparagodānīye namaḥ | pa| oṃ vaṃ uttarakurave namaḥ | u | oṃ yā upadvīpāya namaḥ | a | oṃ rā upadvīpāya namaḥ | nai | oṃ lā upadvīpāya namaḥ | vā | oṃ vā upadvīpāya namaḥ | ī | tathaiva | īṃ yaḥ gajaratnāya namaḥ | īṃ raḥ aśvaratnāya namaḥ | oṃ laḥ puruṣaratnāya namaḥ | oṃ vaḥ strīratnāya namaḥ | oṃ yā khaḍgaratnāya namaḥ | oṃ rā cakraratnāya namaḥ | oṃ lā maṇiratnāya namaḥ | oṃ vā sarvanidhānebhyo namaḥ | ī | oṃ caṃ candrāya namaḥ | da| oṃ sūṃ sūryāya namaḥ | u | oṃ āḥ huṃ śrīvajrasattvagurave namaḥ | madhye | pañcopacārapūjā | oṃ vajragandhe svāhā | gandhaḥ | oṃ vajrapuṣpe svāhā | puṣpaṃ | oṃ vajradhūpe svāhā | dhūpaṃ | oṃ vajranaivedye svāhā | naivedyaṃ | oṃ vajradīpe svāhā | dīpaṃ | oṃ vajralājāya svāhā | lājāṃ | puṣpākṣatasahitajaladhārāṃ maṇḍale pātayet -
body.translated_text: OṂ SULEKHE SARVATATHĀGATĀDHIṢṬHĀNĀDHITIṢṬHANTU SVĀHĀ. Place one flower on the palm, make the hand inverted, and cast it on the <s>maṇḍala</s>. OṂ CANDRĀRKAVIMALE SVĀHĀ. Circumambulate the <s>maṇḍala</s> and cast one flower into the offering vessel. OṂ VAJRASATTVA SARVAVIGHNĀNUTSĀDAYA HŪṂ. Having made two circumambulations beginning from the east, one should perform twenty-one flower-castings on the <s>maṇḍala</s>: OṂ HAḤ — homage to great central <s>Meru</s>! OṂ HRĪṂ — homage to central <s>Meru</s>! OṂ SŪṂ — homage to subtle central <s>Meru</s>! Thus in the center. OṂ YAṂ — homage to <s>Pūrvavideha</s>! [East.] OṂ RAṂ — homage to <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>! [South.] OṂ LAṂ — homage to <s>Aparagodānī</s>! [West.] OṂ VAṂ — homage to <s>Uttarakuru</s>! [North.] OṂ YĀ — homage to the sub-continent! [A.] OṂ RĀ — homage to the sub-continent! [Nai.] OṂ LĀ — homage to the sub-continent! [Vā.] OṂ VĀ — homage to the sub-continent! [Ī.] Likewise: ĪṂ YAḤ — homage to the elephant-jewel! ĪṂ RAḤ — homage to the horse-jewel! OṂ LAḤ — homage to the man-jewel! OṂ VAḤ — homage to the woman-jewel! OṂ YĀ — homage to the sword-jewel! OṂ RĀ — homage to the wheel-jewel! OṂ LĀ — homage to the gem-jewel! OṂ VĀ — homage to all treasuries! [Ī.] OṂ CAṂ — homage to the moon! [South.] OṂ SŪṂ — homage to the sun! [North.] OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ — homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>Guru</s>! [Center.] Five-fold offering (<s>pañcopacārapūjā</s>): OṂ VAJRAGANDHE SVĀHĀ — perfume. OṂ VAJRAPUṢPE SVĀHĀ — flower. OṂ VAJRADHŪPE SVĀHĀ — incense. OṂ VAJRANAIVEDYE SVĀHĀ — food offering. OṂ VAJRADĪPE SVĀHĀ — lamp. OṂ VAJRALĀJĀYA SVĀHĀ — parched grain. One should pour a stream of water with flowers and unbroken rice onto the <s>maṇḍala</s>—

children.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Meru</s> made of four jewels, adorned with eight continents,
Strewn with various jewels — this which grants the unsurpassed,
To the <s>Gurus</s>, the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>, and likewise to the <s>Saṅghas</s>,
I offer with devotion this complete jewel-<s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: stutiḥ | oṃ āḥ huṃ (hūṃ) śrīmadvajrasattvasaguruvaracaraṇakamalāya samyagjñānāvabhāsanakarāya namo 'haṃ namaste 'stu namo namaḥ bhaktyāhaṃ tvāṃ namasyāmi gurunātha prasīda me | kṛtāñjalinā tiṣṭhet |
body.translated_text: Praise: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ — To the lotus-feet of the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s> with the excellent <s>Guru</s>, the cause of the illumination of perfect knowledge — I bow, I pay homage to you, homage, homage! With devotion I bow to you; O Lord <s>Guru</s>, be gracious to me! One should stand with palms joined.

children.translated_text: He by the rays of whose grace the self-reality shines forth,
With retinues of jewel-radiance, by which darkness is dispelled—
Those with unclouded vision see [the truth] playfully and clearly;
To that <s>Guru</s>-sun, this obeisance is made.

children.text: namo buddhāya guruve namo dharmāya tāyine |
children.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Guru</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, the protector!

children.text: namaḥ saṃghāya mahate tribhyo 'pi satataṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the great <s>Saṅgha</s>! Constant homage to all three!
I pay homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and to the <s>Dharma</s> spoken by the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: saṃghaṃ ca śīlasampannaṃ ratnatraya namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: And to the <s>Saṅgha</s> endowed with moral conduct — homage to you, O <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels)!
In the <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels) I take refuge; I confess everything.
I rejoice in the merits of the world; I fix my mind on the <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Buddhas</s>.
Until awakening, I go for refuge to the supreme <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Gaṇa</s> (Community).
I generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) for the accomplishment of the welfare of self and others.
I generate the supreme <s>bodhicitta</s>; I invite all sentient beings.

children.text: iṣṭāṃ cariṣye varabodhicaryāṃ buddho bhaveyaṃ jagato hitāya ||
children.translated_text: I shall practice the excellent conduct of awakening (<s>bodhicaryā</s>); may I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the benefit of the world!
Confession of all sins, and rejoicing in merits,
Having undertaken the observance, I shall practice the noble eightfold <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting observance).
Whatever sin has come upon me, a foolish and deluded one,
Whether naturally wrong, conventionally wrong, or wrong by designation—
That transgression I confess, standing before the Protectors,
With palms joined, frightened by suffering, bowing down again and again.
May the Leaders accept that transgression as a transgression!

children.text: na bhadrakamidaṃ cātha na kartavyaṃ punarmayā ||
children.translated_text: This is not good, and it shall not be done again by me.

body.text: yathā te tathāgatā āryārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā buddhajñānena buddhacakṣuṣā jānanti paśyanti yat kuśalamūlaṃ yajjātikaṃ yannikāyaṃ yādṛśaṃ yatsvabhāvaṃ yallakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the noble <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, know and see with <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge and <s>Buddha</s>-vision the roots of virtue — of what birth, of what class, of what kind, of what nature, of what characteristic—

body.text: yathādharmatayā saṃvidyate | tatkuśalamūlaṃ nityamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitaṃ tathāhaṃ pariṇāmayāmi |
body.translated_text: As they truly exist according to the <s>Dharma</s> — those roots of virtue, always dedicated to the unsurpassed perfect awakening, I too likewise dedicate.

children.text: tathā mamānena samānakālaṃ lokasya duḥkhaṃ ca sukhodayaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Likewise, may I always have the power to remove the suffering of the world and to bring about the arising of happiness,

children.text: hartuṃ ca kartuṃ ca sadāstu śaktistamaḥprakāśaṃ ca yathaiva bhānoḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as the sun has [the power to bring about] darkness and light.
Whether seen, heard, brought to recollection, or encountered through separate narration and contemplation —

children.text: sarvaprakāraṃ jagato hitāya kuryāmajastraṃ sukhasaṃhitāya || iti ||
children.translated_text: in every way, may I ceaselessly act for the welfare of the world, for the sake of happiness. Thus.

body.text: atrāvasare jāpayogaṃ kuryāt | tadāvasāne 'mṛtakuṇḍalivalibhāṇḍe śaṅkhodakaculukaṃ dadyādanena oṃ hrīṃ ācamanaṃ [prokṣaṇaṃ] praticcha svāhā | bhāvanā | tato yaṅkāreṇa vāyumaṇḍalaṃ raṅkāreṇāgnimaṇḍalaṃ tadupari trimuṇḍakṛtacūḍikopari sitapadmabhājanaṃ tatra bhaktādiparipūritaṃ tatropari bruṃ āṃ jiṃ khaṃ huṃ lāṃ māṃ pāṃ tāṃ vaṅkārajātaḥ pañcāmṛtapañcapradīparupaṃ niṣpādya tato garuḍamudrāṃ darśayet | phreṃ 3 | punaḥ śaṅkhodakaculukaṃ dadyādanena - oṃ indrādilokapālebhyaḥ pādyācamanaṃ [nārghaṃ] prokṣaṇaṃ praticcha svāhā | jaḥ huṃ vaṃ horiti mudrāṃ pradarśya indrādidaśadikpālalokapālamudrāṃ ca pradarśya pūrvādikrameṇa balibhāṇḍe puṣpaṃ pātayedebhirmantraiḥ | oṃ indrāya svāhā | oṃ varuṇāya svāhā | oṃ kuverāya svāhā | oṃ agnaye svāhā | oṃ nairṛtye svāhā | oṃ vāyave svāhā | oṃ īśānāya svāhā | oṃ ūrdhvaṃ brahmaṇe svāhā | oṃ adhaḥ pṛthivībhyaḥ svāhā | oṃ sūryāya grahādhipataye svāhā | oṃ candrādi(ya)nakṣatrādhipataye svāhā | oṃ nāgebhyaḥ svāhā | oṃ asurebhyaḥ svāhā | oṃ yakṣebhyaḥ svāhā | oṃ sarvadigvidiglokapālebhyaḥ svāhā | pañcopacārapūjā pūrvavat stutiḥ |
body.translated_text: At this juncture, one should perform the <s>jāpayoga</s> (recitation practice). At its conclusion, one should offer a sip of conch-water into the <s>amṛtakuṇḍali</s> offering vessel with this [mantra]: 'OṂ HRĪṂ — accept the mouth-rinsing [and sprinkling], <s>SVĀHĀ</s>.' Visualization (<s>bhāvanā</s>): Then, with the syllable YAṂ [one generates] the wind-<s>maṇḍala</s>; with RAṂ, the fire-<s>maṇḍala</s>; upon that, atop a <s>cūḍikā</s> (skull-pedestal) formed of three skulls, a white lotus vessel filled with food-offerings and the like. Upon that, BRUṂ ĀṂ JIṂ KHAṂ HŪṂ LĀṂ MĀṂ PĀṂ TĀṂ — having generated from the syllable VAṂ the form of the five nectars and five lamps, one should then display the <s>Garuḍa-mudrā</s> (eagle hand-gesture). PHREṂ (three times). Again one should offer a sip of conch-water with this [mantra]: 'OṂ — To <s>Indra</s> and the other <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Protectors), accept the foot-water, mouth-rinsing, [offering, and] sprinkling, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>.' Having displayed the <s>mudrā</s> JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ, and having displayed the <s>mudrā</s> of the ten directional protectors beginning with <s>Indra</s>, one should cast flowers into the offering vessel in the sequence beginning from the east, with these <s>mantras</s>: 'OṂ — to <s>Indra</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Kubera</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Nairṛti</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — above, to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — below, to the Earth-deities, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), lord of the planets, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to <s>Candra</s> (Moon) and the others, lord of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to the <s>Asuras</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>! OṂ — to all protectors of the directions and intermediate directions, <s>SVĀHĀ</s>!' Five-fold offering (<s>pañcopacārapūjā</s>) as before. Praise:

children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and the other great heroes, the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Protectors) of great supernatural power —
may the ten wrathful ones nail down [obstacles]; homage to you, O removers of obstacles!

body.text: tarpaṇam -
body.translated_text: <s>Tarpaṇa</s> (libation offering) —

children.text: bibhrāṇaṃ buddhabimbaṃ divasakaradhara rāśi yā bindulekham |
children.translated_text: Bearing a <s>Buddha</s>-image, holding a sun[-disc], with the cluster of the <s>bindu</s>-mark,

children.text: maitrīyaṃ cārurūpaṃ śirasi varatanuṃ mañjughoṣaṃ ca gātram ||
children.translated_text: beautiful in form, [representing] <s>Maitreya</s>, with an excellent body, <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> as limbs,
seated on a lotus, in the form of a staff, with an excellent <s>vajra</s>-body, <s>Vajrin</s> (Vajrapāṇi) of fearsome roar —
consciousness in the form of knowledge, which destroys the fear of existence — I bow to the five forms (<s>pañcamūrti</s>).

body.text: sākṣatapuṣpajaladhārāṃ balibhāṇḍe pātayet |
body.translated_text: One should cast a stream of actual flowers and water into the offering vessel.

children.text: indrādivajrī saha devasaṃghairimaṃ ca gṛhṇantu baliṃ viśiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and the others, together with <s>Vajrī</s> (Vajrapāṇi) and the assemblies of gods — may they accept this excellent offering (<s>bali</s>)!
<s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Yama</s> (Death), <s>Nairṛti</s>, the Lord of the Earth, the Lord of Waters, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), and the Lord of Wealth —
<s>Īśāna</s>, the Lord of Beings, the gods above, <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Arka</s> (Sun), and <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Brahmā),

children.text: devāḥ samastā bhuvi ye ca nāgāḥ dharādharā guhyagaṇaiḥ sametāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the <s>devas</s> on earth, the <s>Nāgas</s>, the mountains and the earth, together with hosts of secret beings (<s>guhyagaṇa</s>) —
may they each announce [this offering] in their respective directions, and may the beings in [each] direction

children.text: gṛhṇantu tuṣṭāḥ sagaṇaiḥ sametāḥ sa putradārāḥ saha bhṛtyasaṃghaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: accept [it] satisfied, together with their retinues, with sons and wives, along with the assemblies of servants.

children.text: hṛṣṭāḥ prasannāḥ sraggandhāmālyaṃ puṣpaṃ balirdhūpavilepanaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Delighted and pleased, may they accept the garlands, perfumes, wreaths, flowers, offerings, incense, and ointments;

children.text: gṛhṇantu bhuñjantu pibantu cedaṃ idaṃ ca karmaṃ saphalaṃ bhavenme ||
children.translated_text: may they accept, eat, and drink this — and may this ritual action (<s>karma</s>) bear fruit for me!

body.text: huṃ huṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā punastathaiva ca | oṃ namo ratnatrayāya oṃ caṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahākrodhāya daṃṣṭrotkaṭabhairavāya asimuśalapāśagṛhītahastāya | oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali kha kha khāhi 2 tiṣṭha 2 bandha 2 hana 2 daha 2 paca 2 garjaya 2 tarjaya 2 visphoṭaya 2 mahāgaṇapataye jīvitāntakarāya huṃ huṃ phaṭ 2 svāhā | tatra puṣpādi pūjā | tadvidhiṃ devatāpūjāyāṃ darśaddīpānte lājābhiretadgāthayā pūjayet |
body.translated_text: HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ <s>SVĀHĀ</s>. Again, likewise: 'OṂ — Homage to the <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels)! OṂ — To <s>Caṇḍavajrapāṇi</s>, the greatly wrathful one, terrifying with bared fangs, holding a sword, pestle, and noose in his hands! OṂ <s>Amṛtakuṇḍali</s> — KHA KHA KHĀHI KHĀHI, stand stand, bind bind, strike strike, burn burn, cook cook, roar roar, threaten threaten, burst burst! To the great <s>Gaṇapati</s>, the ender of life! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ <s>SVĀHĀ</s>!' Thereupon, flower-offering and the rest. That procedure [is performed] at the end of the lamp-showing during the deity-worship; one should worship with parched grain (<s>lājā</s>) with this <s>gāthā</s> (verse):

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that arise from a cause — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus has the Great Ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>) spoken.

body.text: pūṣpākṣatajalaiḥ pūjayedanena | oṃ akāro mukhaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmādyanutpannatvāt | oṃ āḥ huṃ (hūṃ) phaṭ svāhā | dakṣiṇā | oṃ mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya taṇḍuladakṣiṇā saṃpraḍho(to)ṣayāmyaham | sākṣatāñjalenā tiṣṭhet | oṃ vajrasattvasamayamanupālaya vajrasattvattvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava sutoṣyo me bhava supoṣyo me bhava anurakto me bhava sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha sarvakarmasu ca me cittaśriyaṃ kuru huṃ ha ha ha ha ho bhagavan sarvatathāgata vajraṃ mā me muñca vajrībhava mahāsamayasattva āḥ | iti gurumaṇḍalakriyā |
body.translated_text: One should worship with flowers, unbroken rice, and water using this [mantra]: 'Oṃ, the letter A is the foremost of all <s>dharmas</s>, because of [their] primordial non-arising. Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā.' The offering (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>): 'Oṃ, to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who is in the form of a youth (<s>kumārabhūta</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), the greatly compassionate one — I offer this rice-<s>dakṣiṇā</s> to please [him].' One should stand with water and unbroken rice in cupped hands: 'Oṃ <s>Vajrasattva</s>, guard [my] <s>samaya</s> (pledge); as <s>Vajrasattva</s>, be present for me; be firm for me; be well-pleased with me; be well-nourished for me; be devoted to me; grant me all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments); and in all actions, make the glory of [my] mind — Hūṃ Ha Ha Ha Ha Hoḥ, O Blessed One, O all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, do not forsake me, the <s>vajra</s>-being! Be the <s>vajra</s>-[nature], O great <s>samaya</s>-being — Āḥ.' Thus [concludes] the <s>Guru-maṇḍala</s> rite.

body.text: tato devatāpūjārthaṃ devatāyā śiraḥpradeśe puṣpamāropya etadbhāvanāvākyaṃ paṭhet | oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho 'ham | oṃ śūnyatājñānavajrasvabhāvātmako 'ham | dhūpavākyam | oṃ bhagavan śrī amukavajravidyārāja namo 'stu te |
body.translated_text: Then, for the purpose of worshipping the deity, having placed a flower upon the head-region of the deity, one should recite this contemplation-formula: 'Oṃ, all <s>dharmas</s> are pure by nature; I am pure by nature. Oṃ, I am of the essence of the <s>vajra</s> of <s>śūnyatā</s>-<s>jñāna</s> (emptiness-wisdom).' The incense formula: 'Oṃ, O Blessed One, glorious <s>Vajra-vidyārāja</s> [of such-and-such name], homage to you!'

children.translated_text: O Lord, compassionate one, I wish to create
a <s>maṇḍala</s> for the sake of compassion toward disciples and for your worship.
O Blessed One, please bestow grace upon me, your devotee.
May the Buddhas, who grant the purpose of the wheel of the world's activity, bless me!
And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who abide in the fruit[-stage], and whatever other <s>mantra</s>-deities,
the deities, the world-protectors, and the beings who have accomplished awakening,
whatever beings delight in the teaching and possess the <s>vajra</s>-eye,
out of compassion toward me together with [my] disciples —

body.text: amukadevatānāmācāryam arcayiṣyāmi | tatra vajradhūpaṃ niryātayāmi tatra vajradhūpaṃ praticcha svāhā | tataḥ sākṣāt puṣpāñjaliṃ dhṛtvaitadadhyeṣaṇāvākyaṃ paṭhet -
body.translated_text: I shall worship the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) of the deities of [such-and-such name]. Thereupon, I offer <s>vajra</s>-incense: 'Accept the <s>vajra</s>-incense — Svāhā.' Then, actually holding a flower-offering in cupped hands, one should recite this entreaty-formula:

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca me |
children.translated_text: Today my birth has become fruitful, and my life has become fruitful.
I have cultivated the <s>samaya</s> (pledge) of all the gods — there is no doubt.
I shall become irreversible (<s>avaivartī</s>), with a mind single-pointed in <s>bodhicitta</s> (the thought of awakening).
Today, birth in the <s>Tathāgata</s> family shall be mine — there is no doubt.

children.text: agro me divaso hyadya yajño me 'dya hyanuttaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Indeed, today is my foremost day; today is my unsurpassed sacrifice.
Indeed today is [my] auspicious assembly, through the invitation of all Buddhas.

body.text: oṃ kusumāñjalinātha horiti mantraṃ paṭhan devatāsannidhau prakiret |
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ, with a flower-offering, O Lord — Hoḥ' — reciting this <s>mantra</s>, one should scatter [flowers] in the presence of the deity.

body.text: tadanu snānavidhiḥ || tatrādau suvarṇādibhājane śubhrasvacchasunirmalakāṃsyadarpaṇaṃ dhṛtvā tatra praṇavamekaṃ suvarṇaśalākayā vilikhya tasminneva jaladhārāṃ pātayedanayā gāthayā -
body.translated_text: Then follows the bathing rite: First, in a vessel of gold or similar [material], having placed a bright, clear, and perfectly pure bronze mirror, one should inscribe a single <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) upon it with a golden stylus, and then pour a stream of water upon it with this verse:

children.translated_text: Oṃ — whatever is the auspiciousness of [him who is] established in the hearts of all beings,
of [him who is] the Self of all, the lord of the noble <s>Dharma</s>-family,
of [him who is] free from all faults without remainder, the one of great bliss —
may that auspiciousness be your supreme consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>)!

body.text: punaḥ pañcāmṛtaiḥ snāpayet | oṃ sarvatathāgata bruṃ āṃ jiṃ huṃ | tataḥ pratibimbaṃ darśayedanena |
body.translated_text: Again, one should bathe [the deity] with the five nectars: 'Oṃ, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — Brūṃ Āṃ Jiṃ Huṃ.' Then one should show the reflection with this [verse]:

children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are like reflections — clear, pure, and undefiled,
ungraspable and unstainable, arisen from causes and actions.

body.text: snānodakamātmanaḥ śirapradeśe 'bhiṣecayet | oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaṃ samāśriye huṃ | iti snānakarmānte jaladhārayā maṇḍaṃ kārayeddevatāsamīpe | oṃ vajrabhūmau surekhe sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhitiṣṭhantu svāhā | oṃ vajrasuvarṇajaladhāre svāhā | sindūreṇābhūṣayet |
body.translated_text: One should anoint one's own head-region with the bathing-water: 'Oṃ, I take refuge in the consecration of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — Hūṃ.' At the conclusion of the bathing rite, one should make a <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) with a stream of water near the deity: 'Oṃ, on the <s>vajra</s>-ground, O well-lined one, may all <s>Tathāgatas</s> consecrate [this] — Svāhā. Oṃ, <s>vajra</s>-golden-water-stream — Svāhā.' One should adorn [the deity] with vermilion.

body.text:
idaṃ te paramaṃ gandhaṃ pavitraṃ ghrāṇatatparam |
dadāmi paramaṃ bhaktyā pratigṛhṇa yathāsukham |
body.translated_text:
This is the supreme fragrance for you, sacred and delightful to the sense of smell;
I offer [it] with supreme devotion — accept [it] at your pleasure.

body.text: oṃ vajragandhe svāhā | oṃ vajratilakabhūṣaṇe svāhā | yajñopavītam | oṃ vajravastrālaṅkārapūjāmeghasamudrasphuraṇayajñopavīta vajrabodhyaṅga dṛḍhakavaca vajravastraṃ svāhā | tato devatāmūlamantreṇāṣṭottaraśatavāraṃ puṣpamabhimantrya (devatāyā śirasi) tatpuṣpaṃ devatābhyaḥ samarpayet |
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>-fragrance Svāhā. Oṃ <s>Vajra</s>-<s>tilaka</s>-ornament Svāhā.' The sacred thread: 'Oṃ, <s>vajra</s>-garment-ornament-worship-cloud-ocean-flashing sacred-thread, <s>vajra</s>-<s>bodhyaṅga</s> (limb of awakening), firm armor, <s>vajra</s>-garment — Svāhā.' Then, having consecrated flowers one hundred and eight times with the deity's root <s>mantra</s>, one should offer those flowers to the deities [upon the deity's head].

children.text: svasti vaḥ kurutāṃ buddhāḥ svasti devāḥ saśatrukāḥ |
children.translated_text: May the Buddhas bring you welfare! May the gods with [their] enemies [vanquished bring] welfare!

children.text: svasti sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvakālaṃ diśantu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May all beings grant you welfare at all times!
By the power of the merit of the Buddhas, and by the will of the deities,
Whatever purpose has been desired — may every purpose be fulfilled today!

children.text: svasti vo dvipade bhontu svasti vo 'stu catuṣpade |
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you who go on two feet; may there be well-being for you who go on four!

children.text: svasti vo vrajatāṃ mārge svasti pratyāgateṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for those traveling on the road; may there be well-being for those returning!

children.text: svasti rātrau svasti divā svasti madhye dine sthite |
children.translated_text: May there be well-being at night, may there be well-being by day, may there be well-being at midday;

children.text: sarvatra svasti vo bhontu mā caiṣāṃ pāpamāgamat ||
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you everywhere; may evil never come upon them!

children.text: sarve sattvāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarvebhūtāśca kevalāḥ |
children.translated_text: May all sentient beings, all living creatures, and all beings without exception

children.text: sarve vai sikhinaḥ santu sarve santu nirāmayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all be happy; may all be free from illness!
May all behold auspiciousness; may evil never come upon anyone!
Whatever beings have assembled here, whether stationed on the earth or in the sky,

children.text: kurvantu maitrīṃ satataṃ prajāsu, divā ca rātrau ca carantu dharmam ||
children.translated_text: may they always practice loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward all creatures, and may they practice the <s>Dharma</s> by day and by night!

body.text: oṃ vajrapuṣpe svāhā | naivedyasamarpaṇam | oṃ vajranaivedya svāhā |
body.translated_text: OṂ <s>VAJRAPUṢPE</s> SVĀHĀ. Offering of <s>naivedya</s> (food offering). OṂ <s>VAJRANAIVEDYA</s> SVĀHĀ.

children.translated_text: OṂ — the food and drink and other [offerings] conforming to the <s>vajra</s>-commitment (<s>vajrasamaya</s>), O Lord,
Endowed with color, fragrance, and flavor — accept [them] at your pleasure!

body.text: atha tarpaṇam -
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation offering) —

body.text:
oṃ namo bhagavate vīravīreśāya huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo mahākalpāgnisannibhāya huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo jaṭāmakuṭotkaṭāya huṃ huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo draṃṣṭākarālograbhīṣaṇamukhāya huṃ huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo sahasrabhujaprabhāsvarāya huṃ huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo paraśupāśatriśūlakhaṭvāṅgadhāriṇe huṃ huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo vyāghracarmāmbaradharāya huṃ huṃ phaṭ |
oṃ namo mahādhūmrāndhakāravapuṣe huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā |
body.translated_text:
OṂ — Homage to the Blessed <s>Vīravīreśa</s> (Lord of Heroes)! HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him who is] like the great fire at the end of an aeon! HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] terrible with the crest of matted locks (<s>jaṭāmakuṭa</s>)! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] of terrible and fearsome face with dreadful fangs! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] radiant with a thousand arms! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] who bears the axe (<s>paraśu</s>), noose (<s>pāśa</s>), trident (<s>triśūla</s>), and skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>)! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] who wears a tiger-skin garment! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Homage to [him] whose body is of great smoky darkness! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!

body.text: godugdhasamarpaṇam |
body.translated_text: Offering of cow's milk.

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgata cintāmṛtadhāre svāhā | dīpārpaṇam |
body.translated_text: OṂ <s>SARVATATHĀGATA CINTĀMṚTADHĀRE</s> SVĀHĀ. Offering of the lamp.

children.translated_text: Pleasing to the eyes, with many jewel-treasuries, with lotus-feet worshipped by kings —
Those who offer garlands of lamps there, where the net of delusion is destroyed by the lamp of knowledge —

body.text: oṃ vajradīpe hrīṃ svāhā | tato mūlamantreṇāṣṭottaraśatavāramantritalājābhirye dharmeti gāthāṃ paṭhitvā devatāṃ prakiret | akāramukhetyādinā baliṃ dattvā | mañjuśriyetyādinā dakṣiṇāṃ ca samarpya sākṣatāñjalinā śatākṣaradhāraṇīṃ paṭhet |
body.translated_text: OṂ <s>VAJRADĪPE</s> HRĪṂ SVĀHĀ. Then, with the root <s>mantra</s>, having empowered parched grains 108 times and having recited the <s>gāthā</s> '<s>ye dharmā</s>' (whatever phenomena arise from causes), one should scatter [them] upon the deity. Having offered the <s>bali</s> (ritual oblation) with '<s>akāramukha</s>' and so forth, and having presented the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) with '<s>Mañjuśriye</s>' and so forth, one should recite the hundred-syllable <s>dhāraṇī</s> with palms joined holding unbroken rice.

body.text: tato 'kṣatārpaṇārthe jalena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra daśapuṣpāṇi pātayedebhirmantraiḥ | oṃ pīṭhāya svāhā | oṃ upapīṭhāya svāhā | oṃ kṣetrāya svāhā | oṃ upakṣetrāya svāhā | oṃ chandāya svāhā | oṃ upachandāya svāhā | oṃ melāpakāya svāhā | oṃ upamelāpakāya svāhā | oṃ śmaśānāya svāhā | oṃ upaśmaśānāya svāhā | tatra pañcopacārapūjāṃ kṛtvā baliṃ dadyāt || oṃ pīṭhopapīṭhakṣetropakṣetrachandopachanda- melāpakopamelāpakaśmaśānopaśmaśānādhivāsino vīravīreśvarīḥ sarvān bhaktitaḥ praṇamāmyaham | tato 'kṣatārpaṇasamaye vakṣyamāṇastotrāṇi paṭhet | oṃ āḥ huṃ (hūṃ) śrīmadvajrasattvetyādinā |
body.translated_text: Then, for the offering of unbroken rice, having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> with water, one should drop ten flowers therein with these <s>mantras</s>: OṂ — to the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>upapīṭha</s> (secondary seat), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>kṣetra</s> (field), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>upakṣetra</s> (secondary field), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>chanda</s> (desire), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>upachanda</s> (secondary desire), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>melāpaka</s> (gathering), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>upamelāpaka</s> (secondary gathering), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>śmaśāna</s> (cremation ground), SVĀHĀ! OṂ — to the <s>upaśmaśāna</s> (secondary cremation ground), SVĀHĀ! Having performed the five-fold worship (<s>pañcopacārapūjā</s>) there, one should give the <s>bali</s> offering. OṂ — I bow with devotion to all the heroes and heroines (<s>vīravīreśvarī</s>) dwelling in the <s>pīṭhas</s>, <s>upapīṭhas</s>, <s>kṣetras</s>, <s>upakṣetras</s>, <s>chandas</s>, <s>upachandas</s>, <s>melāpakas</s>, <s>upamelāpakas</s>, <s>śmaśānas</s>, and <s>upaśmaśānas</s>! Then, at the time of the unbroken-rice offering, one should recite the hymns to be described: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ, beginning with '<s>śrīmadvajrasattva</s>' and so forth.

children.translated_text: The aggregation of omniscient knowledge, the accomplisher of the purposes of the world,
Arisen like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) — homage to you, O glorious <s>Saṃvara</s>!
The great knowledge pervading all, always abiding in the self of all,
Compassionate and wrathful, greatly fierce — homage to you, O glorious <s>Saṃvara</s>!

body.text: ityādi paṭhitvā kṣamārpaṇaṃ kuryāditi | tatra kṣamāpanam | śatākṣaramantroccāraṇānantaraṃ dānapatītyādinā manobhīpsitasaṃkalpavākyānantaramevaṃ kṣamārpaṇaṃ kuryāt |
body.translated_text: Having recited thus and so forth, one should offer the prayer for forgiveness (<s>kṣamārpaṇa</s>). Therein, the request for forgiveness: after the recitation of the hundred-syllable <s>mantra</s>, after the sentence of the desired intention beginning with '<s>dānapati</s>' (patron), one should offer the prayer for forgiveness as follows:

children.text: aprāptena ca prajñānamaśaktaṃ ca mayā vibho |
children.translated_text: O Mighty Lord, by one who has not attained wisdom, by one who is incapable — by me,
Whatever has been deficient or excessive, O Protector — may you forgive all that!

children.text: kṣantumarhantu saṃbuddhā devatā tad vratāśca ye |
children.translated_text: May the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, the deities, and those who observe vows forgive!
May <s>Brahmā</s> and the other world-protectors (<s>lokapāla</s>), and the rites of the spirit-beings, [also forgive]!

children.text: śāntiṃ svastiṃ ca puṣṭiṃ ca bhaktasyānugrahāya ca |
children.translated_text: For the sake of peace, well-being, and prosperity, and for showing grace to the devotee —

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kiñcit mayā mūḍhadhiyā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever misdeeds have been done by me, a fool of deluded mind —

children.text: kṣantavyaṃ ca tvayā nātha yadi trātāsi dehinām |
children.translated_text: May they be forgiven by you, O Protector, if you are the savior of embodied beings!

children.text: kuru dānapateḥ śāntiṃ svastiṃ puṣṭiṃ ca sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: Grant the patron peace, well-being, and prosperity always!

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ kāyajaṃ pāpaṃ vāgjaṃ pāpaṃ ca yatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever sin committed by the body, whatever sin committed by speech,
Whatever sin committed by the mind — all that I hereby confess!

children.text: namo 'stu te buddha anantagocare namo 'stu te satyaprakāśaka mune |
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s>, whose domain is infinite! Homage to you, O sage who illuminates the truth!

children.text: satyapratiṣṭhāya prajāya me ca sarve ca kāryāḥ saphalā bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: May truth be established for me and for all beings, and may all endeavors be fruitful!

body.text: mantrahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ bhāvanāvākyahīnakam | prasīda parameśvara parameśvari rakṣa 2 māṃ koṭi aparādhaṃ kṣamasva | iti kṣamāpya āvāhitadevān visarjayet |
body.translated_text: Whatever is deficient in <s>mantra</s>, deficient in ritual action, deficient in meditation and speech — be gracious, O supreme Lord, O supreme Lady! Protect, protect me! Forgive ten million offenses! Thus having asked forgiveness, one should dismiss the invoked deities.

children.translated_text: Your task is accomplished; having granted the accomplishment of all beings' purposes, go as you will.
Depart to the <s>Buddha</s>-realms, and for the sake of coming again!

body.text: svasvasthāne gacchadhvaṃ | oṃ āḥ huṃ (hūṃ) vajramaṇḍalaṃ mūriti visarjanā |
body.translated_text: Go each to your own abode! OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ — the <s>vajra-maṇḍala</s> form — dismissal.

body.text: iti nityakarmapūjāvidhiḥ samāptaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Nityakarmapūjāvidhi</s> (Procedure for Daily Ritual Worship) is completed.

body.text: sarvasattvārthasiddhirbhavantu ||
body.translated_text: May there be the accomplishment of the welfare of all sentient beings!
